brief: Goldman's daily wrap reports the S&P down 58bps at 7592, up 11% year to date, attributing the move to rising oil and higher yields alongside defensive positioning and worsening sentiment. Levels cited: Brent $108, US 10-year 4.96%, gold $4333, bitcoin $77k, copper down 4% on US tariff headlines, ECB +25bps as expected, Oracle +4% and Adobe -2% post-market, ahead of the US inflation print and next week's Fed decision. Two items argue rather than report. German equities: fiscal stimulus moving from promise to delivery and recovering manufacturing support GS economists' 2027-28 growth acceleration and consensus 17% 2027 EPS growth versus 9% for STOXX 600, leaving the DAX at 15x P/E as a GARP case that is still under-owned, with energy and China the stated risks. US pensions: 112% funded, the highest since 2001, so de-glide and immunisation create potential mechanical equity selling and fixed income buying into quarter-end. The rest is reported: DeepSeek's cheap model and trimmed KV cache, SpaceX conference guidance, $135bn of convertible issuance with AI borrowers at 44%, August PPI +0.4%, a 0.23% core CPI forecast, debt-to-GDP projected at 123% by 2035, and S&P skew in the first percentile.
